And he said to them:
"It is not possible for you to enter the fortress by day;
but when it grows dark, come and you will find the gates open (or: while they are open),
and enter secretly.
And do not bring any of the horsemen with you,
lest the guards perceive it,
and the secret be revealed;
rather let the horsemen lie in ambush nearby."
And when the Prince believed this,
he set out from 'Ayna and pretended that he was going to Antioch.
And when evening came,
he returned, together with his wife, his son, and the young servants who were attending them.
And they approached the gate and found it open,
and they entered with joy.
And the governor said to them:
"Sleep now and rest until daybreak,
so that we may make an arrangement,
and bring in some of the horsemen little by little,
and seize the guards."
And while they were asleep,
the governor sent to Leo, who was lying in ambush there;
and he came with a multitude of Armenians,
and entered Baghras and seized the Prince,
and bound him (and weighed him down) with fetters,
and also cast irons upon his wife and his son.
And he inflicted severe torments upon him,
in place of the torments which that Prince had inflicted upon Roupen, Leo's brother.
And the Prince remained a prisoner with Leo,
until Henry came, the sister's son of the King of England,
and through persuasions and covenants released him.
And Leo was greatly strengthened after the death of Sultan Qilij Arslan,
and took seventy-two fortresses,
some of them from the Turks,
and some of them from the Greeks.
And in all his battles he was seen to be victorious.
Now 'Izz al-Din Mas'ud, the lord of Mosul,
when he heard that Saladin had died,
desired to restore to himself the kingdom of Syria.
And he sent to 'Imad al-Din his brother, {OCR?} the lord of Sinjar and Nisibis,
and to Sinjar Shah, the son of his brother, the lord of the city of Jazira,
and to Muzaffar al-Din ibn Zayn al-Din, the lord of Erbil;
and he prepared them so that they might march together,
and take away the cities from the house of Saladin.
Now al-Malik al-Afdal, the eldest son of Saladin,
who had reigned in Damascus in his father's place,
he also sent to his uncle al-'Adil,
who was at that time in Harran {OCR? Damascus in text, likely error for Harran/Karak or repeating Damascus},
and brought him with urgency to him so that he might stand at the head of the forces,
and encounter the house of the Atabeg.
